registry.policy: This registry is the single inventory of PXAPI v1 contracts. Every contract carries its own version, and that version is the semantic authority for that contract alone: the registry version below describes the shape of this file, never the meaning of a contract listed in it. Registering a contract is an additive change — it never alters the meaning of a contract already listed — and requires no change to the validation harness, which derives its whole inventory from this data.

problem_codes.meaning: A document does not satisfy the contract it claims; errors names each violated constraint by JSON pointer and schema keyword. It is also the code for a document that declares no schema_version at all: an absent version is a missing member, not an unsupported one.
The requested contract is not registered in this registry. The requested name is not echoed back, because it is untrusted input.
The document declares a schema_version that is present but is not the version this contract pins. A document that omits schema_version is CONTRACT_VALIDATION_FAILED instead.
A caller asked for an Analysis Run state transition that is not an approved edge of the coarse execution lifecycle. The two states are named; nothing else about the run is carried.

problem_code_policy: This list names the codes registered at this point in the delivery sequence. problem.code is an open token: a later slice registers further codes here without changing the version of the problem contract, and adding a code never alters the meaning of an existing one. A client must treat an unknown code as a generic problem of the given title and detail rather than reject the document.
